title: Placebo Response, Causal Inference, and Ethics
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
In a clinical trial, people assigned to a placebo group may improve. Calling all of that change “the placebo effect,” however, hides several processes. Symptoms can fluctuate naturally; people often enter a study when symptoms are unusually severe and later move closer to their typical level; measurement and reporting can change; participants may receive supportive care; and expectations or the treatment ritual may alter experience. The broad *placebo response* is the observed change in a placebo group. A causal *placebo effect* is the part attributable to the context or meaning of treatment, which requires an appropriate comparison—often including a no-treatment or differently framed condition.

Context can produce measurable effects, especially for outcomes such as pain, nausea, or anxiety. Learning, expectation, attention, and interaction with a clinician may influence perception and behavior, and some experiments identify associated neural or physiological pathways. This does not mean that expectation removes every disease process. A change in reported pain and a reduction in tumor size, for example, are different outcomes. Good reasoning defines the endpoint before deciding what has improved.

Randomization helps make treatment groups comparable on average, while blinding reduces ways that knowledge of assignment can influence behavior, care, reporting, or assessment. A placebo-controlled trial estimates the difference between an intervention and its comparator under the study conditions; it does not literally subtract every psychological influence from a person. Blinding may also fail when side effects reveal who probably received the active treatment. Researchers must therefore examine whether the blind was credible, whether missing data differed between groups, and whether the chosen comparator answers the clinical question.

Placebo controls are not automatically ethical or unethical. When withholding effective treatment creates serious risk, an active-control or add-on design may be more appropriate: all participants receive standard care, and the experimental treatment or placebo is added. The scientific desire for a clean contrast does not override informed consent, risk minimization, or clinical welfare. At the same time, respectful communication is not a deceptive “extra drug.” It is part of good care. The rigorous conclusion is modest: expectations and context can affect some outcomes, but their size, mechanism, durability, and clinical importance must be tested rather than assumed.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Every improvement in a placebo group is caused by expectation.

options.label: B
options.text: Placebo research requires separating observed response, causal effect, trial design, and ethics.

options.label: C
options.text: Blinding removes all bias from every clinical trial.

options.label: D
options.text: A placebo can replace effective treatment whenever researchers want a clean comparison.

questions.answer: 正解：B。観察された反応、文脈に帰属できる因果効果、試験設計、倫理を区別します。Aは自然変動、Cは盲検破綻、Dは参加者保護を無視します。

questions.prompt: How does a placebo response differ from a causal placebo effect?

options.label: A
options.text: A response is all observed change in the placebo group; an effect is the portion causally attributable to treatment context through an appropriate comparison.

options.label: B
options.text: They are identical names for expectation alone.

options.label: C
options.text: A response excludes natural fluctuation and supportive care.

options.label: D
options.text: An effect can be identified without any comparator.

questions.answer: 正解：A。responseには自然経過、平均への回帰、支持療法なども含まれ、effectは適切な比較で文脈・期待へ因果帰属できる部分です。B～Dはその区別を消します。

questions.prompt: The word “withholding” in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to

options.label: A
options.text: not providing something that could otherwise be given

options.label: B
options.text: measuring an outcome twice

options.label: C
options.text: revealing group assignment

options.label: D
options.text: improving communication

questions.answer: 正解：A。ここでは本来利用できる有効治療を対照群へ与えずにおくことです。B～Dは測定・盲検・意思疎通であり語義が異なります。

questions.prompt: Why does improvement after enrollment at unusually severe symptoms not prove an expectation effect?

options.label: A
options.text: Extreme baseline values may naturally move closer to a typical level even without an intervention.

options.label: B
options.text: Every symptom remains perfectly constant without expectation.

options.label: C
options.text: Time change alone identifies its psychological cause.

options.label: D
options.text: A no-treatment comparison would make causal reasoning weaker.

questions.answer: 正解：A。極端な値が次回測定で通常値へ近づく平均への回帰があり、無治療比較なしでは期待へ帰属できません。B～Dは時間変化を因果の証明と誤認します。

questions.prompt: Why does the passage distinguish reported pain from tumor size?

options.label: A
options.text: To prevent generalizing improvement in one defined endpoint into proof that every disease process or lesion has disappeared

options.label: B
options.text: To show that all subjective and objective outcomes are identical

options.label: C
options.text: To prove expectation always shrinks tumors

options.label: D
options.text: To argue that endpoints need not be defined before analysis

questions.answer: 正解：A。ある症状指標の改善から病因や客観的病変すべての消失へ飛躍する誤りを防ぎます。B～Dは評価項目ごとの測定と臨床的意味を無視します。

questions.prompt: Which limitation of blinding is identified in the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Side effects may allow participants or researchers to guess assignment.

options.label: B
options.text: Randomization guarantees that every individual is identical.

options.label: C
options.text: Placebo controls directly measure every component of healing.

options.label: D
options.text: Missing data cannot bias a blinded trial.

questions.answer: 正解：A。副作用で割付を推測できると行動・報告・評価が変わり得ます。Bは群平均と個人、Cは差の推定と全成分分解を混同し、Dは欠測バイアスを無視します。

questions.prompt: Why does an active-treatment versus placebo comparison not make the whole placebo response a causal placebo effect?

options.label: A
options.text: Placebo-group change mixes natural history, regression to the mean, observation, and supportive care; the group difference estimates the intervention's added effect.

options.label: B
options.text: Every change in the placebo group is necessarily caused by belief.

options.label: C
options.text: The comparison separately identifies every psychological and biological process.

options.label: D
options.text: Natural history and missing data cannot affect either group.

questions.answer: 正解：A。プラセボ群内変化は複数原因の混合で、薬群との差は薬の追加効果を推定しても群内変化を全原因へ分解しません。B～Dは識別範囲を誇張します。

questions.prompt: What principle is expressed by saying that a clean scientific contrast does not override consent, risk minimization, or welfare?

options.label: A
options.text: A highly informative design is unacceptable if it exposes participants to excessive risk; active-control or add-on designs may be needed.

options.label: B
options.text: Scientific clarity always justifies withholding effective treatment.

options.label: C
options.text: Ethics and research design are unrelated.

options.label: D
options.text: Consent can be omitted whenever a placebo is used.

questions.answer: 正解：A。識別力の高い設計でも過大な危険を課せず、必要なら実薬対照・上乗せ設計を選びます。B～Dは研究目的を参加者保護より優先します。

questions.prompt: What is wrong with concluding that a 30% placebo-group improvement proves belief cured 30% of the disease?

options.label: A
options.text: The percentage describes change, not cause; alternative processes and the endpoint must be separated with an appropriate comparison.

options.label: B
options.text: Within-group change always identifies both mechanism and biological cure.

options.label: C
options.text: Supportive care, natural fluctuation, and regression to the mean can be ignored.

options.label: D
options.text: A symptom score and the underlying disease are necessarily the same endpoint.

questions.answer: 正解：A。30%は群内変化であって原因ではなく、自然変動、平均への回帰、報告、支持療法を比較で分け、何が改善したか定義する必要があります。B～Dは因果を飛躍させます。
